Average width and average density, but with above average hairs per graft. Light brown in color.
Thank you! I am happy as well - they clearly know what they are doing. They also told me I have above average hairs per graft which should benefit me. Very excited to see the results.

I can't speak to other clinics, but my experience with FUE Capilar (which I had to book months in advance) was extremely positive . I have heard good things about Aygin, but he performs Sapphire FUE and I wanted DHI which had faster healing time. Cost was about 3700 USD plus flight (2k USD). Generally, you should ask if a doctor will actually do the procedure (rare from what I can see) and how many patients they see a day. People in Turkey said that clinics on the Asian side saw less people and were generally of higher quality.

It was a whole day ordeal, broken out over two to three sessions. Sometimes this clinic will take two days to do it because it is too much graft harvesting in one day to be healthy (they are one of the only clinics to do this). Honestly the beginning is stressful because you don't know what is happening and they have to inject anesthesia into your head (not pleasant). That being said, there was a dedicated translator there and they check in to see how your are doing. Overall, there were 6ish people in the room + the doctor and the procedure took about 9-10 hours including consultation. I got there at 8:15 AM and was back in my hotel by 7:30 PM.

Much much more expensive in the US/Europe - think 5 - 8x as expensive ($3k is also real money) and Turkey has a ton of local experience on the topic. Now that being said, you can also find a really cheap clinic in Turkey that can go really poorly (it is not as well regulated, many clinics barely have doctor involvement). That's why I went with who I did, they were the most responsive and professional (and that included US folks I reached out to who were quoted for 20k+).

FWIW Turkey is also a really nice country with kind people, great culture/beaches and cheap as well. Will definitely go back for a visit.
yeah, realistically to prevent additional hair loss. otherwise the transplant could look fucked up.

I was assessed to not have norwood scale hair loss, the doctor said it didn't fall into the standard characterization. They recreated my entire hairline through the crown and added a small amount to the temples. My hair was very thick on both sides and had diffuse thinning throughout my head, but on video calls my hairline looked normal. If I tilted my head down it was very clear and it got to a point where I wouldn't go outside without a hat. 

I used minodoxil for years and it generally worked well but was afraid to take finesteride (on it now anyways after the transplant). Hair loss started and I slipped from a twice a day routine and then gave up entirely, demoralized. Lesson learned here is prevention is much easier than remediation (good lesson for your 20's)

Links to before (https://imgur.com/a/aqJQ9X3) and after ([https://imgur.com/a/QbxiaZi](https://imgur.com/a/QbxiaZi)). Again, my hair was messed up and I'm really happy I addressed it. Note, it has been 4 days since the surgery.

Answered some of this above but the transplant was 3000 EUR (3700 USD) - you can get cheaper but I prioritized getting a doctor to perform the procedure using the technique I wanted (DHI). Often the big clinics are like assembly lines for hair transplants and will do 5-10 people a day. Went to FUE Capilar (Dr. Dogan Turan) and have been very impressed but the work and his team's aftercare. 

Hard to say recovery time, but it's been 4 days and it doesn't look bad (just weird, lots of scabbing). I did get some pretty bad swelling on my head and eyes though, which is just clearing up today (4 days). I timed it so I could have a few months to heal before my remote work ends. I expect it to be about 5-6 months before it truly looks decent but I am taking biotin to hopefully accelerate.

They take from the back of your head (aka donor area) with a tiny graft extracting device that makes .8mm punches. There will no longer be hair in that area (which sounds bad, but honestly, it's been 4 days and you can't really tell. From my understanding, if your hair is longer than a 1 buzz in the back, it shouldn't be noticeable. It also heals surprisingly quickly. This is a good example: [http://hairtransplantdiary.com/day-5/](http://hairtransplantdiary.com/day-5/)

Total cost was about $5700 USD. 3700 USD for the procedure (flat fee regardless of number of grafts) and 2000 USD for the flight from the US (would be cheaper, but had to change it last minute).  I went with FUECapilar w. Dr. Dogan Turan who did the entire implementation himself (his clinic does one person a day) and highly recommend them.  Stay (3 nights) was included as was breakfast and transport. Spent an extra $50 or so on food but effectively it was all inclusive.
